subject: Deployment mode sift & PoC timeline — MedOps AI
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elena Russo <elena.russo@medops.ai>; Samir Patel <samir.p@medops.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + decision criteria for deployment mode

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned before we build the PoC plan: 

Summary of needs you stated on the call:
- Data residency and internal audit requirements (SOC2 + encrypted logs) for any production path.
- Peak inference latency target: 150 ms p50 for single-request interactive UI.
- Expected avg daily tokens: ~15M (spikey weekdays).
- Hard constraint: no model weights hosted by public multi-tenant tenants for PHI workflows (so private or dedicated preferred unless host allowed).

Deployment modes to consider (and pros/cons):
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding) — lowest time-to-value, managed fallbacks and streaming, but multi-tenant model hosting may not meet your policy for PHI unless contractually isolated.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools with tenancy isolation and predictable throughput; good fit if you want Redwood-managed infra but isolated for compliance.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — full customer control, integrates with KMS/HSM, best for the strictest compliance but longer lead time and ops responsibility.

Proposed PoC approach (two-week pilot window):
- Phase 0 (3 days): Confirm data subset, success criteria, and test harness (we’ll use the spreadsheet attached).
- Phase 1 (7 days): Run sample traffic against a Hosted API variant and a Dedicated variant (same model family) to compare latency, cost, and quality.
- Phase 2 (4 days): If Dedicated is clearly superior for isolation and latency at scale, provision a short Dedicated slot and run longer load tests; otherwise validate Hosted with contractual & network controls.

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency p50 <= 150 ms and p95 < 600 ms under expected concurrency.
- No PSI/PHI leakage in outputs (we’ll run your prompt set and evaluate).
- Cost target: under $0.006 per 1k tokens (PR ballpark — we’ll refine).
- Compliance: acceptance of SOC2 evidence and KMS integration options.

Next steps / asks for MedOps team:
1) Elena — confirm which of the three deployment modes is a hard requirement vs preference.
2) Samir — share a 200–500 prompt evaluation set and the performance-weighted concurrency estimate.
3) Procurement — confirm your typical PO/contract cadence so we can plan Dedicated provisioning timelines.

I attached a PoC requirements worksheet and a short pricing sketch — loop back with any edits and we’ll produce a formal two-week runbook.

Thanks —
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Russo <elena.russo@medops.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + decision criteria for deployment mode

Diego —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We cannot host PHI-bearing workloads on any public multi-tenant environment unless we have contractual isolation and audit logs that prove tenant separation. That makes Hosted API possible but low-confidence unless you offer a contractual guarantee.
- Dedicated capacity sounds like the sweet spot operationally, provided you can guarantee the latency SLOs at our concurrency.
- Private VPC is acceptable but will add procurement and infra lead time; we'd like to avoid it if Dedicated meets compliance.

Samir will send over the prompt set by tomorrow EOD. Procurement is cc’d; they will reply with typical SLA add-ons and PO timelines.

Elena
Head of Product | MedOps AI

Elena / Samir —

Thanks — good to have procurement in the loop. Two small updates after reviewing your prompt set (Samir) and internal compliance note: 

- Based on the prompt set and hit rates, we estimate 12–18M tokens/day during trial (aligns with your projection). We modeled both Hosted and Dedicated paths for cost and perf — short summary attached (Redwood_Pricing_Sketch.pdf).
- Hosted API option: we can offer a contractual isolation addendum (tenant isolation + access logs) that covers PHI-style controls for the pilot; it still remains a shared infra model but with stronger controls for audit.
- Dedicated option: provisioning lead time is typically 7–10 business days after contract (for a short reserved slot) — can be accelerated for a paid expedite.
- Private VPC: 4–6 weeks typical (networking + compliance checks).

Recommended pilot: Run a split-PoC: first 1 week on Hosted (with the contractual addendum and strict telemetry enabled) and simultaneously run baseline tests on a short Dedicated slot for a day of peak load testing. That gives you both the fastest signal and a representative Dedicated comparison without committing to long lead times.

Proposed timeline:
- Aug 20 (Thu): Procurement confirms PO cadence / redline owners.
- Aug 24 (Mon): We deliver the formal two-week runbook and access tokens.
- Aug 25–Sep 7: PoC window (split testing as above).
- Sep 8: Results & recommendations call.

Action items for Redwood (I’m taking point, cc Marissa/Ben):
- Produce runbook and a dedicated short-slot quote (Marissa will draft the pricing).
- Prepare SOC2 evidence packet and the contractual isolation addendum (Ben).

Could Marissa and Ben confirm they can hit the Aug 24 runbook delivery?

Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
